q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings release is scheduled for August 26, 2026 (tomorrow from the question date of August 25, 2026). This is essentially **resolved or about to be resolved** — we're asking for the forward guidance that will be announced in approximately 24 hours.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** (which would be for Q3 FY2027, the October quarter), not the Q2 results themselves.

Key data points from the research:
- **NVIDIA's prior guidance** for Q2 FY2027 revenue was $91.0B ± 2% ($89.2B-$92.8B), issued in May 2026
- **Wall Street consensus** for Q2 FY2027: ~$91.9B (42 analyst estimates)
- **Citi analysts specifically project** $105 billion for the October quarter (Q3 FY2027)
- The research notes that NVIDIA guidance explicitly excludes China Data Center compute revenue

The most likely scenario is that NVIDIA will provide guidance in the **$100B-$110B range** for Q3 FY2027, based on:
1. Citi's specific $105B projection for the October quarter
2. Historical sequential growth patterns in NVIDIA's data center business
3. The fact that guidance typically reflects strong demand continuation

The research explicitly cites Citi analysts projecting "$105 billion for the October quarter," which is the forward guidance period in question.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Unexpected deterioration in demand signals during the Q2 call
- New geopolitical restrictions on China sales impacting guidance
- Macro weakness or AI infrastructure spending pullback
- Weaker-than-expected customer orders post-earnings
- Inventory concerns or channel weakness

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Stronger-than-expected bookings/backlog during Q2
- Expanded TAM in new AI application areas
- Better-than-anticipated supply chain normalization
- Positive guidance from major cloud customers
- Additional data center capacity availability

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides **one explicit forward guidance projection**: Citi analysts project **$105 billion for the October quarter**. This is the only named, specific forecast for the forward guidance period in the provided research.

Historical NVIDIA growth rates aren't provided in the research, but the cited guidance range of $89.2B-$92.8B for Q2 FY2027 (vs. ~$91.9B consensus) shows typical guidance accuracy within 2-3% of results.

Given that Citi is specifically cited as projecting $105B for the October quarter, and this represents a reasonable ~15% sequential growth from the $89-93B Q2 range, this appears to be a credible analyst view.

## Final Estimate

The most direct evidence points to **$105 billion** as a reasonable central estimate for forward guidance. The range provided ($99.5B-$115.5B) brackets this fairly tightly. I expect NVIDIA to guide toward the higher end of typical sequential growth patterns given strong AI demand.

Accounting for:
- Citi's $105B projection (specific evidence)
- Uncertainty around exact guidance (companies may go higher or lower than analyst consensus)
- The range provided encompasses $99.5B-$115.5B
- Historical 2-3% guidance accuracy within known ranges

NVIDIA is scheduled to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, after the U.S. market close, with the analyst call following at 2 p.m. PT [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026), [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8).

NVIDIA's own guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued in May 2026, is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, creating a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/), [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026). This guidance explicitly "is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China" [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/).

Wall Street's consensus estimate, based on 42 analyst estimates compiled by Yahoo! Finance, is approximately $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). The Zacks consensus estimate is slightly lower at $91.8 billion, meaning NVIDIA would need to land in the upper half of its own guided range to meet expectations [piptheory.com](https://piptheory.com/research/nvidia-q2-fy2027-earnings-preview-august-2026). Citi analysts, however, expect NVIDIA to report $93 billion in revenue for the July quarter and project $105 billion for the October quarter [finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/analyst-rethinks-nvidia-stock-ahead-163300755.html).
